notes: §1985:VII.4.3.2 prints OPEN followed by a repeatable choice of INPUT { file-name-1 [ REVERSED | WITH NO REWIND ] } ..., OUTPUT { file-name-2 [ WITH NO REWIND ] } ..., I-O { file-name-3 } ... and EXTEND { file-name-4 } .... openStatement is OPEN openClause+, openClause an openMode and openFileSpec+, and openFileSpec a name with (REVERSED | WITH? NO REWIND)?, one phrase at most; the superset rule offers the phrase after every mode, and BindOpen cuts it to the printed positions through CheckOpenTapePhrase and the two OpenTapePhraseRule rows: REVERSED in the INPUT group only (COBOL2211) and on a record sequential file only (COBOL2210, §1985:VII.4.3.3 SR1), NO REWIND in the INPUT and OUTPUT groups only (COBOL1803). ResolveFile refuses a qualified, subscripted or reference-modified file-name (COBOL2972) and a name that is no file (COBOL1639). The 1985 edition keeps REVERSED through VisitOpenFileSpec, silent at 85 and COBOL0902 from 2002, and refuses the later phrases through VisitOpenStatement (SHARING) and VisitRetryPhrase (RETRY), both COBOL0900. Probed at 85: every form of the format compiles, the modes repeated and mixed in one statement, a different phrase per file-name, WITH written or dropped; OPEN OUTPUT, I-O and EXTEND with REVERSED, I-O and EXTEND with NO REWIND, REVERSED WITH NO REWIND on one file, a mode with no file-name, a file-name with no mode, WITH REWIND, WITH LOCK, IO and INPUT-OUTPUT as modes are refused. At run time OPEN INPUT F1 REVERSED delivers the records last to first and OPEN EXTEND appends. The witness opens OUTPUT (two files), EXTEND, I-O and a mixed INPUT F1 F2 OUTPUT F3 statement, and compiles INPUT ... REVERSED, INPUT ... WITH NO REWIND and OUTPUT ... WITH NO REWIND.

next.reason: §1985:VII.4.3.2 opens sequential files INPUT with an optional REVERSED or WITH NO REWIND per file, OUTPUT with an optional WITH NO REWIND, and I-O and EXTEND with none. §2023:14.9.27.2 keeps the four modes, the repeated mode groups and '[ WITH NO REWIND ]' per file, and §2023:14.9.27.3 SR5 ('The NO REWIND phrase may be specified only for sequential files') and SR6 ('The NO REWIND phrase may be specified only when the INPUT or OUTPUT phrase is specified') keep it where the 1985 format put it. But there is no REVERSED phrase (in 1985 obsolete, §1985:VII.4.3.3 SR1 'The REVERSED phrase can only be used with sequential files'), so OPEN INPUT f REVERSED is refused at compile time; and the sharing-phrase and retry-phrase are added. Narrower and wider: CHANGED.
